title: Wire full-stack integration tests into CI and SDLC pipeline
summary: Architecture analysis for gating PRs with integration tests in GitHub Actions CI and enabling egg's tester agent to run full-stack integration tests during the SDLC pipeline. Phase 1 adds pull_request triggers to existing reusable workflows and fixes the test-integration.yml build step. Phase 2 introduces orchestrator-managed DinD for SDLC self-testing. Recommended approach: Option A (add PR triggers directly) for Phase 1, Option C (orchestrator-managed DinD sidecar) for Phase 2.

problem_statement.description: 91+ integration tests exist across 8 files in integration_tests/local_pipeline/ with full infrastructure (compose files, mock sandbox, fixtures), but none run automatically on PRs. The three test/lint workflows (test.yml, lint.yml, test-integration.yml) are workflow_call-only with no callers on pull_request events. Additionally, test-integration.yml only builds the gateway image, not the orchestrator. For SDLC self-testing, the tester agent sandbox has no Docker access, making it impossible to run full-stack tests from within the pipeline.
goals: Make lint.yml, test.yml, and test-integration.yml run on every PR
Fix test-integration.yml to build both egg-gateway and egg-orchestrator images
Build and tag mock-sandbox image in CI before running local pipeline tests
Make test results visible as PR checks
Enable egg's tester agent to run full-stack integration tests via DinD sidecar
Preserve the on-check-failure.yml autofix naming dependency
Maintain sandbox trust model (no Docker socket in sandbox)

ci_workflows.mechanism: 16 workflow files. test.yml, lint.yml, test-integration.yml are reusable (workflow_call + workflow_dispatch only). PR-triggered workflows are limited to code review (on-pull-request.yml), contract verification, agent-mode-design review, and action tests (test-action.yml, path-filtered).
ci_workflows.key_limitation: No workflow triggers test/lint/integration on pull_request events. on-check-failure.yml (autofix) watches for workflow names 'Lint' and 'Test' via workflow_run event — these names must be preserved.
ci_workflows.autofix_dependency: on-check-failure.yml line 8: workflows: ['Lint', 'Test']. If tests run as jobs within a caller workflow named 'CI', the workflow_run event fires for 'CI' not 'Lint'/'Test', breaking autofix.

integration_tests_root.mechanism: Gateway-only compose stack for gateway integration tests (test_gateway_*.py, test_network_*.py, etc.). Used by existing test-integration.yml cleanup step.
integration_tests_root.test_count: Multiple test files at integration_tests/ root level testing gateway auth, network isolation, policy enforcement, rate limiting, etc.

local_pipeline_tests.mechanism: Full-stack compose (gateway + orchestrator) with mock-sandbox. 91+ tests across 8 files. Session-scoped fixture builds mock-sandbox image, starts compose with --build, waits for health, yields stack URLs, tears down.
local_pipeline_tests.compose_services: gateway (built from gateway/Dockerfile) + orchestrator (built from orchestrator/Dockerfile). Uses test subnets 172.40.x/172.41.x.
local_pipeline_tests.mock_sandbox: Alpine + curl + phase-runner.sh (310 lines). Supports role-based behavior (checker, reviewer, worker) and failure injection via env vars/prompt keywords.
local_pipeline_tests.fixture_lifecycle: conftest.py: generate config -> build mock-sandbox -> docker compose up -d --build -> wait health (120s each) -> yield -> dump logs -> docker compose down -v

test_integration_workflow.mechanism: Builds only egg-gateway image. Runs pytest integration_tests -v -m 'integration or security' --timeout=300. Cleanup references integration_tests/docker-compose.yml (gateway-only stack).
gaps: Does not build egg-orchestrator image (needed by local_pipeline tests)
Does not build mock-sandbox image (fixture builds it, but pre-building improves cache and failure clarity)

sandbox_trust_model.mechanism: Sandbox containers get no Docker socket. All Docker operations (container spawning, network management, volume mounts) are orchestrator-driven. Gateway sessions pre-registered before spawn, updated with container IP after startup.
sandbox_trust_model.constraint: Sandbox must never receive Docker socket access. Integration tests requiring docker-compose must run either on CI runners (Phase 1) or via DinD managed by the orchestrator (Phase 2).

devserver_manager.mechanism: Manages Docker compose stacks for deployment validation during check phase. Extracts compose config from committed state, generates override with readonly code mounts, creates air-gapped network, starts/stops stack. Enforces resource limits (1 CPU, 512MB RAM, 256 PIDs, 5-min timeout).
devserver_manager.relevance: Demonstrates the pattern for orchestrator-managed container stacks without giving sandbox Docker access. Phase 2 DinD approach follows a similar architecture but spawns a nested Docker daemon instead of services directly.

docker_client.mechanism: DockerClient respects DOCKER_HOST env var: explicit parameter > env var > default socket auto-detection. Supports any valid Docker daemon URL (unix socket, TCP, SSH).
docker_client.relevance: Phase 2 DinD: sandbox tester would set DOCKER_HOST=tcp://dind:2375 to connect to the nested daemon. DockerClient already supports this without code changes.

approaches.name: Add PR triggers directly to reusable workflows
approaches.description: Add `on: pull_request` trigger to lint.yml, test.yml, and test-integration.yml alongside the existing workflow_call trigger. Fix test-integration.yml to build both gateway and orchestrator images. This is the simplest path to get all tests running on PRs. GitHub Actions supports dual triggers (workflow_call + pull_request) on the same workflow.
pros: Minimal changes — 3 workflow files modified, no new files
Workflow names preserved ('Lint', 'Test', 'Integration Tests') so on-check-failure.yml autofix works
workflow_call compatibility maintained for future callers
Docker natively available on ubuntu-latest — no special setup
Local pipeline fixture already handles full compose lifecycle (build, start, wait, teardown)
cons: If another workflow calls them via workflow_call on PRs, they run twice (unlikely in practice)

approaches.name: Create caller ci.yml workflow
approaches.description: Create a new ci.yml workflow triggered on pull_request that calls lint.yml, test.yml, and test-integration.yml via workflow_call. Reusable workflows remain purely reusable.
pros: Clean separation — reusable workflows stay purely reusable
Single place to manage PR checks
cons: BREAKS autofix: on-check-failure.yml watches for 'Lint' and 'Test' workflow names. Called workflows run as jobs within the caller, so workflow_run events fire for 'CI' not 'Lint'/'Test'
Would require modifying on-check-failure.yml to watch for 'CI' and then figuring out which job failed

approaches.name: Orchestrator-managed DinD sidecar for SDLC self-testing
approaches.description: For the tester agent in the SDLC pipeline, the orchestrator spawns a docker:27-dind-rootless sidecar container. The orchestrator pre-loads mock-sandbox and test images into the DinD daemon. The tester sandbox receives DOCKER_HOST=tcp://dind:2375 and runs integration tests against a nested test stack. Follows the same trust model as DevserverManager — orchestrator manages infrastructure, sandbox only runs tests.
pros: Enables full-stack integration tests from within SDLC pipeline
Preserves sandbox trust model (no Docker socket in sandbox)
DockerClient already supports DOCKER_HOST env var
Nested test stack fully isolated from production
cons: Significant orchestrator complexity: DinD lifecycle, image pre-loading, network bridging
DinD startup adds latency (daemon init + image load)
Requires --privileged or specific device access for DinD container
New test fixture needed to detect and adapt to DinD environment

approaches.name: Orchestrator runs tests directly (no sandbox involvement)
approaches.description: The orchestrator itself executes pytest for integration tests, since it already has Docker socket access.
pros: Orchestrator already has all necessary Docker access
cons: VIOLATES trust model: test execution runs arbitrary code from agent changes in the trusted orchestrator
Test failures or resource leaks could destabilize the orchestrator
Tightly couples test execution to orchestrator internals

recommended_approach.name: Phase 1: Add PR triggers (Option A), Phase 2: DinD sidecar (Option C)
justification: Phase 1 (Option A) is the highest-value, lowest-risk change: 4 files modified to gate all PRs with lint, unit tests, and integration tests. Workflow names preserved so autofix works.

Phase 2 (Option C) is the only approach that enables SDLC self-testing while preserving the sandbox trust model. Option D is rejected for violating trust boundaries. DevserverManager provides architectural precedent.
Option B is rejected because it breaks the on-check-failure.yml autofix workflow naming dependency.
Phases are fully independent — Phase 1 provides immediate value even if Phase 2 is deferred.

technical_decisions.decision: Add pull_request triggers directly to reusable workflows (not a caller ci.yml)
technical_decisions.rationale: GitHub Actions supports dual triggers (workflow_call + pull_request). Adding pull_request directly preserves the workflow names ('Lint', 'Test', 'Integration Tests') which is critical for on-check-failure.yml autofix. A caller ci.yml would change the workflow_run event name to 'CI', breaking autofix.
alternatives_considered: Caller ci.yml workflow (Option B) — rejected due to autofix naming break

technical_decisions.decision: Pre-build all Docker images explicitly in test-integration.yml before running pytest
technical_decisions.rationale: While the conftest.py fixture builds mock-sandbox and compose builds gateway+orchestrator via --build, pre-building in CI provides: (1) better caching via Docker layer cache, (2) clearer failure messages if a build fails, (3) faster re-runs since images are cached. The conftest fixture should detect pre-built images and skip redundant builds.
alternatives_considered: Rely entirely on conftest fixture to build images — works but slower and less debuggable in CI

technical_decisions.decision: Use docker:27-dind-rootless for Phase 2 DinD sidecar
technical_decisions.rationale: docker:27-dind-rootless is the standard Docker-in-Docker image. Rootless mode reduces attack surface. The orchestrator (which has Docker socket access) manages the DinD container lifecycle, preserving the trust model. The sandbox connects via TCP (DOCKER_HOST=tcp://dind:2375) without needing Docker socket access.
alternatives_considered: Orchestrator runs tests directly (Option D) — rejected: violates trust model
Give sandbox Docker socket access — rejected: fundamental security violation
Use Sysbox or other container runtime — adds dependency, not worth complexity

technical_decisions.decision: DinD image pre-loading via docker save/load over TCP
technical_decisions.rationale: The DinD daemon is a fresh Docker instance with no images. The orchestrator must pre-load required images (egg-gateway, egg-orchestrator, mock-sandbox) before the tester can run compose. docker save on the host daemon piped to docker load on the DinD daemon is the standard approach and works reliably over TCP.
alternatives_considered: Pull images from registry within DinD — requires registry access, may not work in private mode

technical_decisions.decision: Integration tests should initially be non-required PR checks, promoted to required once stable
technical_decisions.rationale: Integration tests have never run in CI before. There may be environment-specific failures on ubuntu-latest that don't occur locally. Making them immediately required could block all PRs. Start as informational checks, monitor for stability, then promote to required via branch protection rules.
alternatives_considered: Immediately required — risky if tests are flaky in CI
Always optional — defeats the purpose of gating

technical_decisions.decision: Phase 2 DinD follows DevserverManager architectural pattern
technical_decisions.rationale: DevserverManager (orchestrator/devserver.py, 1028 lines) already solves an analogous problem: running Docker compose stacks for validation without giving sandbox Docker access. DindManager follows the same separation: orchestrator provisions infrastructure, sandbox interacts via HTTP/TCP (not Docker socket). This provides tested architectural precedent.
alternatives_considered: New bespoke architecture — rejected: unnecessary when proven pattern exists

risks.description: Integration tests may be flaky or fail on ubuntu-latest due to Docker timing, network subnet conflicts, or architecture differences (development host is Linux 6.17 aarch64 Asahi/Fedora vs ubuntu-latest x86_64).
risks.mitigation: Start with non-required checks. Add retry logic or increase timeouts for CI. Run integration tests manually via workflow_dispatch first to validate before enabling PR triggers.

risks.description: Adding integration tests to every PR increases CI time by 5-10 minutes, slowing development velocity.
risks.mitigation: Consider path-based filtering to only run integration tests when gateway/, orchestrator/, shared/, or integration_tests/ files change. Use Docker layer caching (actions/cache) to speed up image builds.

risks.description: Phase 2 DinD sidecar adds significant orchestrator complexity. DinD container may fail to start, images may fail to pre-load, networking between sandbox and DinD may be unreliable.
risks.mitigation: Phase 2 is independent of Phase 1. Build DinD management as a separate, well-tested module (DindManager). Add integration tests for DinD lifecycle before wiring into production orchestrator. DevserverManager provides tested pattern to follow.

risks.description: on-check-failure.yml autofix may not handle integration test failures well since they involve Docker/compose issues that are harder to auto-fix than lint or type errors.
risks.mitigation: Integration test autofix is opt-in (task-1-4). Can be removed if autofix proves ineffective for Docker-related failures.

risks.description: DinD requires --privileged flag which expands the attack surface of the orchestrator-managed containers.
risks.mitigation: Use rootless DinD (docker:27-dind-rootless) which reduces privilege requirements. DinD container is managed by the trusted orchestrator, not the untrusted sandbox. DinD container runs on an isolated network and is torn down after tests complete.

risks.description: Dual triggers (workflow_call + pull_request) on the same workflow could cause double runs if another workflow calls them on PR events.
risks.mitigation: No existing workflows call lint.yml, test.yml, or test-integration.yml on PR events. on-check-failure.yml only calls autofix on workflow_run completion, not on PR events. Risk is theoretical.

constraints: Sandbox containers must never receive Docker socket access (trust model)
Workflow names 'Lint', 'Test', 'Integration Tests' must be preserved for on-check-failure.yml autofix
workflow_call compatibility must be maintained on all reusable workflows
GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest has Docker natively available (no special setup needed)
Phase 1 and Phase 2 are fully independent — Phase 2 can be deferred without blocking Phase 1 value
The conftest.py fixture currently builds mock-sandbox and starts compose — CI should pre-build for caching but fixture should still work standalone
Two compose stacks exist: integration_tests/docker-compose.yml (gateway-only) and integration_tests/local_pipeline/docker-compose.yml (full-stack). Both need cleanup in CI.

Q1_required_checks.question: Should integration tests be required PR checks immediately, or start as informational and promote after validation?
Q1_required_checks.recommendation: Start informational, promote after stability is confirmed (TD-5)

Q2_autofix_integration.question: Should on-check-failure.yml also watch for 'Integration Tests' failures to trigger autofix?
Q2_autofix_integration.recommendation: Yes, add it — autofix can attempt to fix code issues that cause integration test failures. Easy to remove if ineffective.

Q3_phase2_scope.question: Is Phase 2 (SDLC self-testing via DinD) in scope for this issue, or should it be a follow-up?
Q3_phase2_scope.recommendation: Phase 2 is significantly more complex. Recommend Phase 1 first, Phase 2 as follow-up or deferred scope. The issue explicitly requests both phases but they are independent.

Q4_path_filtering.question: Should integration tests only run on PRs that modify gateway/, orchestrator/, shared/, or integration_tests/ code?
Q4_path_filtering.recommendation: Start without path filtering (run on all PRs) to catch unexpected regressions. Add path filtering later if CI time becomes a concern.
